items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: But in order to be able to write Stravinsky, Schoenberg, that kind of stuff, he went to school.

ctx.x: Well he actually said it was a guy named John Cotter who was — he was the musical director for Della Reese. And he learned a lot of the big band stuff there. And then he worked with a lot of the regional bands, Jeter-Pillars and a lot of the bands in the St.

Louis-Kansas City area. There were several funeral directors, and I can’t remember some of the names of some of these guys, but they had big bands and Dad played there. So he learned how to write there. But in order to be able to write Stravinsky, Schoenberg, that kind of stuff, he went to school. And that’s when he went to study at Washington University.
Okay. I just wanted to tell you that I don’t know if you know that your father made the 1960 edition of Leonard Feather’s book.
